title: Sharp finite noise contraction
statement:
Let $I$ be a finite set with real weights satisfying $\sum_iw_i=1$, and let $q>2$ and $0<\lambda<1/2$, with $w_i\ge\lambda$ for every $i$. Put $p=q/(q-1)$ and let $\rho$ be the sharp discrete radius at $(q,\lambda)$. Then every $f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfies
\[
\rho^2\sum_iw_i f_i^2+(1-\rho^2)\left(\sum_iw_i f_i\right)^2\le\left(\sum_iw_i|f_i|^p\right)^{2/p}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: $\rho$ is the sharp discrete radius at $(q,\lambda)$
replaced: Let $I$ be finite, let $\sum_iw_i=1$, let $q>2$, $0<\lambda<1/2$, and assume $w_i\ge\lambda$ for all $i$. Put $p=q/(q-1)$ and $\rho=\rho_*(q,\lambda)$. Every real vector $f$ satisfies $\rho^2\sum_iw_if_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_if_i)^2\le(\sum_iw_i|f_i|^p)^{2/p}$. Here $\rho_*(q,\lambda)=\sqrt{\sinh(\ell/q)/\sinh(\ell/(q/(q-1)))}$ with $\ell=\log((1-\lambda)/\lambda)$.
